intro:
If you searched "AthenaHQ free trial," you're probably trying to test the tool before committing real money — and that's a reasonable thing to want from any AI-visibility platform. The short version: there isn't a free trial to find. AthenaHQ is a premium, paid-first product.

This page lays out exactly what it costs to get in the door, why reviewers flag the entry price as steep for small teams, and what your options are if you only want to see where you stand right now — without a contract or a credit card.

sections.heading: The direct answer: no free trial, no free tier
sections.body:
AthenaHQ does not publish a free trial or a free-forever plan. To use the platform, you subscribe to a paid plan first. The lowest-cost entry point is the **Self-Serve plan at $295/month**, which includes a set monthly credit allotment (around 3,600 credits, where each tracked AI response consumes one credit) and coverage across the major engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, Claude, and Copilot.

The one concession to trial-seekers is a **discounted first month** — commonly cited at roughly 67% off, landing around $95–$97 instead of $295. That's genuinely cheaper, but it's important to be clear about what it is and isn't: it's a discounted *paid* month, not a free trial. You enter payment details and pay upfront before you see a single result. If you cancel, you've still paid for that first month.

sections.heading: Why the entry price gets flagged in reviews
sections.body:
Independent reviews of AthenaHQ repeatedly note the same thing: the commitment is high *just to evaluate the tool*. There's no way to kick the tires for $0. For a well-funded marketing team or agency, $295/month (or a $95 first month) is a rounding error and the depth of analytics may justify it quickly.

But for **solopreneurs, small teams, and people who only want a quick look** at their AI visibility, that's a real barrier. You're asked to pay before you know whether the tool surfaces anything useful for your specific brand and queries. Two other points reviewers raise, in fairness to your decision: the Self-Serve plan is limited to a **single country**, and the credit-based model means your effective cost scales with how much you actually track — so the bill can be less predictable than the $295 sticker suggests. Some premium features, like the ACE Citation Engine and API/BI integrations, are **Enterprise-only**.

sections.heading: What AthenaHQ is genuinely good at
sections.body:
To be fair, the price buys real capability — this isn't a thin product. AthenaHQ is built for ongoing, serious AI-search monitoring: tracking visibility across nine-ish models, citation intelligence (which sources the AI engines pull from when they mention you or competitors), competitor benchmarking, blindspot detection, dynamic crawling, and role-based team access. It's designed for teams that want **historical dashboards, continuous tracking, and depth** rather than a one-time snapshot.

If your job is to manage AI visibility as an ongoing channel — with stakeholders, reporting, and a budget to match — that depth is the point, and the discounted first month is a low-risk way to evaluate it. The friction is purely that you can't see any of it without paying first.
